answer: Give each applicant one kite tethered to a single bridge pylon, keyed to its key, one per pylon. The registry releases seven gust challenges; each gust's target is folded from the last tension reading plus the key, so each gust opens only after the last reading is filed. The applicant logs line tension as the zephyr crosses; a replayed log never matches a fresh gust, since each pylon's shear is its own. At the seventh gust the kite dips over a dune marker. Each extra identity burns a $290 rig and 26 flight-hours; 8,000 impostors would owe $2.32 million and 208,000 flight-hours.
